subject: Short-term sandbox fuel request: 10k RPS POC smoke run
messages:
From: Ethan Huang <ethan@lumenhealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: devops@lumenhealth.com
Date: 2026-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick ask — short burst credits for 10k RPS smoke run

Hi Camila,

We’re planning a short, high-concurrency smoke run next Tuesday to validate end-to-end latency and throughput for the search assistant POC. The team wants to drive roughly 10k RPS at peak for a 6-hour window (we’ll ramp over 90 minutes and then hold).

Can Redwood provide a temporary sandbox supplement (promotional credits / ephemeral quota) and a 48-hour trial extension so we can include the final soak and post-run analytics? We expect ~1.2M inference requests (mostly short chats) and estimate ~450k tokens for the run — happy to share more detailed load profiles.

Attached is our short POC plan (lumen-poc-plan-2026-08-19.pdf) with timing and expected traffic shape. Key ask: credit allocation and confirmation of autoscale settings (we’ll need to allow bursts and KV cache warmup).

Appreciate any options — we’re on a tight validation window and would like to lock resources by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Ethan Huang
Senior Platform Engineer
LumenHealth

Attachment: lumen-poc-plan-2026-08-19.pdf (PDF, 340KB)

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-19T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — short burst credits for 10k RPS smoke run

Hi Ethan — thanks for the plan. I reviewed the attachment quickly and this is doable but we need to lock a couple of operational items before we provision credits.

Can you confirm the exact start/end UTC window and whether you’ll run synthetic traffic from a single region or distributed generators? That affects routing and the autoscale profile. Assuming the 6-hour peak and your token estimate, my preliminary recommendation is a temporary promotional allocation enough for 600k generated tokens and a 48-hour trial extension so you can do post-run analysis and a small re-run if needed.

I’m looping in Marcus (runtime infra) and Marissa (customer success) to confirm we can reserve the ephemeral pool and validate warmup steps. I’ll attach an internal ops checklist for our CS/infra handoff. If finance sign-off is required for the promo, I’ll escalate after we confirm the final numbers.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm exact UTC window and generator topology (city/region)
- Marcus confirms ephemeral pool sizing and autoscale config
- I request credits and a 48-hour extension from promotions/billing

If that all looks good, I can aim to get a provisional allocation by Monday EOD.

— Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

On Wed, Aug 19, 2026 at 10:37 AM Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I’m looping in Marcus (runtime infra) and Marissa (customer success) to confirm we can reserve the ephemeral pool and validate warmup steps.

We can stand up an ephemeral GPU pool for a 12-hour allocation window and keep a small reserved headroom for the KV cache warmup. For a 10k RPS peak across short-chat prompts, the simplest configuration is: 4 x A100-equivalent workers with autoscale capped to 8 workers for burst safety. That should give the throughput and keep latency within SLOs if the input length stays under 64 tokens most of the time.

Operational notes:
- Recommend 90-minute ramp with prefix caching enabled and steady-state cache retention set to 45 minutes.
- Enable continuous batching with max batch size tuned to 128 tokens; this will reduce per-token cost without blowing latency.
- We can pre-warm the KV cache with a short 60-minute synthetic run the night before (low volume) — this reduces tail latency during the main window.

If Camila requests a provisional credit amount, I’d advocate for a conservative promo allotment that covers a failed re-run (so ~1.25x expected token usage). Happy to jump on a 15-min call to sync on sizing.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
